children: JPMorgan Chase

fluctuated between a modest gain and small losses Tuesday after the bank's Q3 earnings and revenue missed Wall Street consensus estimates. Its Q3 commercial and investment banking results softened markedly from Q2's robust pace. Each line of business, though, grew from the year-ago quarter.

The U.S.'s largest bank by assets saw its consumer banking unit's earnings and revenue continue to grow. It also benefited from a lower-than-expected provision for credit losses and higher-than-expected net interest income.

The company now expects 2026 net interest income, excluding markets, of ~$97.2B vs. its prior guidance of $96.5B, with ~$25.5B of that in Q4. Overall, the bank expects NII of ~$106.2B, market dependent, compared with the Visible Alpha consensus of $105B and its previous outlook of $105B.
For 2007, the company expects net interest income, excluding markets, of $107B for its base case, with growth driven by the impact of balance sheet growth and higher rates, the company said.

FY2026 adjusted expenses are now expected to be ~$108.6B, compared with its prior guidance of ~$107.5B and the Visible Alpha estimate of $108.4B. Card service net charge-off rate is expected to be ~3.2% compared with its previous estimate of 3.2%.
, vs. the average analyst estimate of $5.94, decreased from $6.14 in Q2 and increased from $5.07 in last year’s Q3.
Adjusted revenue of $50.9B, trailing the $51.2B consensus, dropped from $58.0B in the prior quarter and climbed from $47.1B a year ago.

In discussing the quarter's results, Chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon said, "Our capital hierarchy has remained consistent over time, with investing in the franchise and supporting our clients at the top. In line with our hierarchy, we reduced share repurchases this quarter. We believe we can deploy this capital over time at very attractive returns for our shareholders."
Q3 return on common equity of 17% compared with 24% in the previous quarter and 17% a year ago.
Provision for credit losses was $2.74B, lower than the Visible Alpha consensus of $2.83B, compared with $2.52B in the previous quarter and $3.40B a year ago.
Net interest income (managed) of $27.1B, beating the Visible Alpha consensus of $26.9B, grew from $25.6B in Q2 and $24.1B in Q3 2025.
JPMorgan Chase’s
total loans at Sept. 30, 2026, grew to $1.58T from $1.54T at June 30, 2026. Deposits, at $2.78T, rose from $2.71T at the end of Q2.
Q3 noninterest expense of $27.3B vs. the $27.3B Visible Alpha estimate was unchanged from Q2 and increased from $24.3B in last year’s Q3.
Q3 revenue and net income by segment:
Consumer & Community Banking net revenue of $21.2B grew 4% Q/Q and 9% Y/Y; net income of $5.67B advanced 7% Q/Q and 13% Y/Y.
Commercial & Investment Banking revenue of $22.7B fell 9% Q/Q and increased 14% Y/Y; net income of $8.25B slid 15% Q/Q and jumped 20% Y/Y

Investment Banking fees of $3.0B rose 14% Y/Y. Markets & Securities Services revenue of $11.8B grew 13% Y/Y. Markets revenue of $10.3B rose 15% Y/Y. Fixed Income & Markets revenue of $5.4B fell 4% Y/Y. Equity Markets of $5.0B drove up 49% Y/Y.

Asset & Wealth Management revenue of $6.91B increased 1% Q/Q and 14% Y/Y; net income of $1.84B fell 6% Q/Q and rose 11% Y/Y. Assets under management came to $5.2T, up 13%, and client assets of $7.9T climbed 15%, driven by continued net inflows and higher market levels.
Conference call at 8:30 AM ET.

title: JPMorgan stock wavers after Q3 earnings disappoint as markets soften
